ratings_why.fun: Watching a fish earn its stamps, then sliding it forward to spawn and pour its stats into a neighbour is a lovely turn-by-turn growth story, though the passport bookkeeping is heavy.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the front row means 'go home now', so every move while recruiting is a life-or-death call, and a spent fish's stats pass to its neighbours. No other tribe today turns slot choice into a unit's life cycle like that.

verdict_why: The fantasy reads through the mechanics and needs no rethink, but the homecoming chain can loop forever and two cards need clearer wording.

points.text: Old Bradán loses his Stamps but stays, so Thumbprint Parr's Spawn (doubled by Little Jack Gravel) can refill him to Home 5 in the same chain and he comes home again, with no end. Add 'once a turn' to his Spawn, or say each unit comes home at most once a turn.
Rust-Flank Hen: 'it gains +1/+1' could mean the Hen or the stamped fish. Name the one meant, e.g. 'that unit gains +1/+1'.
Say whether a Spawn set off by Bradán counts as 'spawning' for the Bend-Wife, Little Jack Gravel and Mother Redd's count, and whether a Fry keeps its Stamps when it turns back into a fish.
Reunion Secretary's year-class rule takes a long read. Something like 'Run units with the same Stamps as another Run unit gain +1/+1' keeps the old-school-year joke and reads in one go.

The fantasy really shows in play: back row as resting pools, front row as the home bend, stats feeding whoever stands by the redd. A visible passport pip and a 'going home tonight' marker would make it readable at a glance.

standouts.why: Mother Redd's spared runs are the 'third run, and she mentions it' joke made into rules: her +2/+2 steps grow each time she comes home.
Little Jack Gravel never earns a Stamp yet turns up at every spawning. The fish's story and his rules line up exactly.
The Bailiff stamps everyone's passport and now and then eats a pilgrim. It's the engine, the flavour and the risk on one readable line.

weakest.why: Reunion Secretary: year-classes with a tie-break are the hardest text in the tribe to read.
Fish-Pass Keeper is a plain number tweak with no story or decision of its own.
Pilgrim Guide: 'Spawn: gain 2 gold' is fine, but nothing about the fish shows in what it does.

flags.note: Bradán plus Parr Spawns (doubled by Jack) can bring him home again and again in one End of Turn chain, with no end.
'It gains +1/+1' doesn't say which unit gains.
Doesn't say whether the fresh copy keeps the Fry's Stamps, which decides whether it comes home again at once.
Stamps never cap in the hoard build, so the Attack Llyn Llyw gives every unit keeps climbing.
A copy every turn makes triples of any passported unit cheap, as the designer notes.
